# Tottertop

> Tottertop is a one-tap physics stacking game for phones, now in development. A swaying crane drops blocks onto a wobbling tower; stack it as high as you can. One round takes about a minute.

Tottertop is a single-player mobile game by ipe() (https://ipe.rest/). It is in development and has NOT been released: no store page, release date or final price exists yet. This site is the game's home page.

## Key facts

- Simple physics stacking game, single player.
- One tap to play; a round lasts about one minute.
- Completely free, with no ads and no purchases to remove them.
- Launching on iPhone first, in 12 languages.
- Coming to the App Store. Android later.

## Pages

- [Home](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/): Tottertop is a quick physics game for your phone. A crane swings above a wobbling tower: tap once to drop the block and try to stack it so the tower stays balanced. One round takes about a minute.

## Journal

RSS: https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/feed.xml

- [A short game on purpose: why a round takes about a minute](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-26-a-short-game-on-purpose/): Tottertop is built to fit a short break. Why a round lasts about a minute, and what we have not measured yet.
- [The first round, and a reason for one more](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-25-the-first-round-and-the-next/): Three short tips for a first-time player, a banner the moment you pass your best, and one number on the result screen. Small things added to Tottertop on November 15.
- [Telling the blocks apart: a color-blind check](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-24-telling-the-blocks-apart/): When block color sets arrived in Tottertop, a color-blindness simulation found two default blocks that looked almost the same. What we measured and what we changed.
- [iPhone first, and what iCloud sync does](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-23-iphone-first-icloud/): Tottertop is planned for iPhone only at first. Your progress can follow you between devices on one Apple ID through iCloud, while settings stay on each device.
- [Why Tottertop is meant to be free, with no ads](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-22-free-and-no-ads/): Tottertop is planned as a fully free game: no ads, no rewarded ads, no in-app purchases and no remove-ads option. What that rule changes in the design.
- [Why this journal posts once a day](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-21-one-post-a-day/): Tottertop's journal appears about once a day, in twelve languages. What we write here, what we leave out, and why we do not promise dates.
- [What we test before anything ships](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-20-what-we-test-first/): A short tour of the checks Tottertop goes through before a build leaves the desk: unit tests, a 320 px layout test in 12 languages, bot runs, and what only a real phone can tell us.
- [Sound switched on, nothing heard: the iPhone silent switch](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-19-the-silent-switch/): Turning on sound in Tottertop's settings did nothing on an iPhone with the silent switch on. What caused it, what we changed, and what is still unchecked on real devices.
- [Twelve languages, one fixed order](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-18-twelve-languages-one-order/): Tottertop moved from eleven languages to twelve common ones in a fixed order. What changed, what we dropped, and the narrow-screen test that guards it.
- [The “Perfect” that was not: three fixes from day one](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-17-the-perfect-that-was-not/): On the first full evening of testing Tottertop, three bugs showed up around the “Perfect” landing and the record. What they were and how we fixed them.
- [One tower for everyone: how the daily seed works](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-16-one-tower-for-everyone/): In the test builds, the daily tower hands every player the same block order on the same day. How a date becomes a tower, and why UTC.
- [Tuning the wobble with bots instead of hands](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-15-tuning-the-wobble-with-bots/): How we set Tottertop's difficulty before anyone had played it: three bots with different tap timing, 200 rounds each, and an honest caveat.
- [Why we moved from a dark night sky to mint and sky](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-14-why-mint-and-sky/): Tottertop started dark: a navy night sky with gold. After a polish pass that still looked the same, we switched to a bright, cute mint-and-sky look.
- [What Tottertop is, and why we are making it](https://tottertop.ipe.rest/journal/2026-11-10-what-tottertop-is/): A one-tap physics tower stacker: a crane drops blocks onto a wobbling tower, and one round takes about a minute. Why ipe() is making a game this small.

Every post is available in all 12 languages, each under /<code>/journal/ (English at /journal/).

## Languages

The site is available in 12 languages (English and Korean are written by hand, the others are AI translations): English, 한국어, 日本語, 繁體中文, Español, Português (Brasil), Français, Deutsch, Bahasa Indonesia, ไทย, Tiếng Việt, Türkçe. Each language lives under /<code>/ (English at the root).
